metadata.description: Cross-reference mapping Romance chapters to historical events, highlighting fiction vs. fact

chapter_title.zh: 宴桃园豪杰三结义 斩黄巾英雄首立功
chapter_title.en: Oath of the Peach Garden and First Victory Against Yellow Turbans

historical_period.era: Late Eastern Han - Yellow Turban Rebellion

historical_events_covered.notes: Rebellion historically occurred in 184 CE, widespread peasant uprising

characters_introduced.portrayal_accuracy: moderate - basic facts correct, details embellished

fiction_vs_fact.fact: Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei were close companions and allies
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: The specific oath ceremony in a peach garden is not recorded in historical sources
fiction_vs_fact.source_note: Records mention their relationship but no oath ceremony
fiction_vs_fact.cultural_significance: Iconic scene representing loyalty and brotherhood in Chinese culture
fiction_vs_fact.why_added: Establish theme of loyalty; create dramatic founding moment for their alliance

fiction_vs_fact.scene: Three heroes fighting Lü Bu (三英战吕布)
fiction_vs_fact.fact: Lü Bu was a powerful general; Liu Bei's forces did encounter him
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: This specific three-on-one duel is not recorded
fiction_vs_fact.why_added: Demonstrate martial prowess; establish Lü Bu as formidable opponent
fiction_vs_fact.note: This scene actually appears in later chapters, not chapter 1

fiction_vs_fact.fact: Liu Bei did participate in suppressing Yellow Turban Rebellion
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: Specific battles and tactics are dramatized

literary_devices.technique: Humble origins rising to defeat rebellion

themes_introduced: Mandate of Heaven (serving legitimate Han Dynasty)

chapter_title.zh: 七星坛诸葛祭风 三江口周瑜纵火
chapter_title.en: Zhuge Liang Prays for Wind at Seven Star Altar; Zhou Yu Sets Fire at Three Rivers

historical_events_covered.notes: Battle occurred, but many details are fictional

fiction_vs_fact.scene: Zhuge Liang prays for east wind (借东风)
fiction_vs_fact.fact: Wind direction favored the alliance's fire attack
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: Zhuge Liang summoning wind through ritual is supernatural invention
fiction_vs_fact.source_note: Historical records mention favorable wind but no prayer ritual
fiction_vs_fact.cultural_significance: One of most iconic scenes in Chinese literature
fiction_vs_fact.why_added: Elevate Zhuge Liang to quasi-supernatural status; demonstrate Mandate of Heaven
fiction_vs_fact.symbolic_meaning: Heaven's favor towards the righteous cause

fiction_vs_fact.scene: Fire attack on Cao Cao's fleet
fiction_vs_fact.fact: Fire attack was key tactic that destroyed Cao Cao's fleet
fiction_vs_fact.source: sanguozhi-records, Book of Wu, Biography of Huang Gai

fiction_vs_fact.fact: Zhou Yu was supreme commander of allied forces
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: Novel diminishes his role compared to Zhuge Liang
fiction_vs_fact.historiographical_note: Historically Zhou Yu deserves primary credit; novel shifts credit to Zhuge Liang

historical_divergences.historical_truth: Zhou Yu was supreme commander and chief strategist
historical_divergences.novel_portrayal: Zhuge Liang portrayed as mastermind, Zhou Yu secondary
historical_divergences.reason: Novel written from Shu perspective; elevates Shu figures
historical_divergences.impact: Distorts public perception - many believe Zhuge Liang led Red Cliffs campaign

historical_divergences.historical_truth: Natural weather conditions favored fire attack
historical_divergences.novel_portrayal: Zhuge Liang summons wind through magical ritual
historical_divergences.reason: Add supernatural legitimacy to Shu cause; create memorable scene
historical_divergences.cultural_note: Reflects Daoist influence in Chinese culture

themes: Intelligence and strategy over brute force
Sacrifice for greater good (Huang Gai's feigned surrender)

related_chapters.title: Guan Yu releases Cao Cao at Huarong Road

chapter_title.zh: 刘先主遗诏托孤儿 诸葛亮安居平五路
chapter_title.en: Liu Bei Entrusts His Heir to Zhuge Liang; Zhuge Liang Defends Against Five Armies

name.en: Death of Liu Bei at Baidi Castle

historical_events_covered.notes: Event occurred but dialogue likely embellished

fiction_vs_fact.scene: Liu Bei entrusts Liu Shan to Zhuge Liang
fiction_vs_fact.fact: Liu Bei did entrust his son and kingdom to Zhuge Liang before death
fiction_vs_fact.source: sanguozhi-records, Book of Shu, Biography of Zhuge Liang
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: Exact words and dramatic dialogue are literary invention

famous_quote.zh: 若嗣子可辅，辅之；如其不才，君可自取
famous_quote.en: If my son is worthy, support him; if not, you may take the throne yourself
famous_quote.historical_basis: Similar sentiment recorded in Records, exact words uncertain

fiction_vs_fact.significance: Demonstrates Liu Bei's trust and Zhuge Liang's loyalty

fiction_vs_fact.scene: Liu Bei's death at Baidi Castle
fiction_vs_fact.fact: Liu Bei died at Baidi Castle in 223 CE after defeat at Battle of Yiling
fiction_vs_fact.context: Defeated in campaign to avenge Guan Yu's death

fiction_vs_fact.scene: Five-army invasion defended by Zhuge Liang
fiction_vs_fact.fact: Zhuge Liang did face multiple threats after Liu Bei's death
fiction_vs_fact.fiction: Specific five-pronged attack may be dramatized or consolidated
fiction_vs_fact.purpose: Demonstrate Zhuge Liang's strategic brilliance in crisis

emotional_impact: Climactic end to Liu Bei's arc
Transfer of responsibility to next generation
Zhuge Liang's loyalty demonstrated through acceptance

historical_context.preceding_event: Battle of Yiling defeat (夷陵之战)
historical_context.political_situation: Shu Han vulnerable after Liu Bei's death and earlier losses
historical_context.zhuge_liang_role: Became regent and dominant political force in Shu

most_accurate_content_types: Births and deaths of major figures

accuracy_scoring.high: Core events and outcomes historically confirmed
accuracy_scoring.moderate: Events occurred but details embellished or uncertain
accuracy_scoring.low: Largely fictional with minimal historical basis
accuracy_scoring.fictional: No historical record, pure literary invention

methodology.verification_process: Cross-reference novel chapters with historical records, identify divergences, document reasons for fictional additions
